decisions.quote: Analyses not conducted in Newman et al. (2010) (Handbook of Employee Engagement: Perspectives, Issues, Research, and Practice, pp. 43–61) were performed to deconstruct the explained variance in work engagement into commonality coefficients representing all possible subsets of variables.
decisions.reason: To re-test the redundancy claims of Newman et al. (2010, 2011), the authors did not collect a new sample of job attitude and work engagement data, but instead re-analyzed the original meta-analytic correlation matrix from Newman et al. (2010) using commonality analysis.

decisions.quote: First, the study tested the claim suggested by Newman et al. (2011) (Human Resource Development Quarterly, 22, 37–47) that data from the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale appears to be redundant with the variance that is uniquely common to job satisfaction, affective organizational commitment, and job involvement.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target 1 correctly identify Newman et al. (2011) (DOI 10.1002/hrdq.20065) as a primary target whose claim of redundancy between the UWES and job attitudes is explicitly re-tested.

decisions.quote: The findings demonstrate that variance uniquely common to job satisfaction, affective organizational commitment, and job involvement did not dominate the regression effect as previously suggested.
decisions.reason: Under the corrected reproduction type, decomposing the variance in work engagement into commonality coefficients shows that variance uniquely common to the three job attitudes is only 16.6% (28% of explained variance), debunking Newman et al.'s (2011) redundancy claim (robustness challenges), while computational reproduction is explicitly attributed to the Newman et al. (2010) baseline model rather than separately established for the 2011 paper in the partial excerpts (cannot_be_determined).

corrected_value.title: Job attitudes and employee engagement: Considering the "A-factor".
corrected_value.authors: Newman, D. A., Joseph, D. L., & Hulin, C. L.

decisions.quote: Analyses not conducted in Newman et al. (2010) (Handbook of Employee Engagement: Perspectives, Issues, Research, and Practice, pp. 43–61) were performed to deconstruct the explained variance in work engagement into commonality coefficients representing all possible subsets of variables.
decisions.reason: Newman et al. (2010) is an omitted reproduction target: the authors explicitly re-estimated its structural equation model (Figure 4.3, Panel A) on its meta-analytic correlation matrix, recovering identical latent correlations, and then decomposed the model's variance to challenge its substantive conclusions regarding construct redundancy.
